decisions.reason: After two years on the market, this software remains highly visible and tightly aligned with the firm's publicly stated move toward integrated, data-driven airport operations, so management is likely to continue backing it.

Because this connectivity module builds directly on the established airport systems offer and supports digital integration across apron operations, management would tend to interpret any uneven uptake as temporary and persist with it.

Although billing software is somewhat less central than operational and safety tools, it still extends the firm's software and service scope, so prior investment and strategic commitment make withdrawal possible but still less likely than continuation.
Resource management is close to the firm's core airport operations business and fits its push toward more automated end-to-end solutions, which encourages continued support rather than reversal.

A controller safety alert service is strongly connected to the firm's safety-critical positioning in tower and airside operations, so accumulated commitment and strategic fit make near-term withdrawal unlikely.
